descriptionChirho: Hamath (also transliterated Chamat/Chamath), a major ancient city and kingdom on the Orontes River in modern-day Syria, serving as a key geographical marker for the northern boundary of the Promised Land and Israelite territory. The phrase 'the entrance of Hamath' (לְבוֹא חֲמָת) functions as a standard boundary formula throughout the Hebrew Bible. Appears across multiple biblical contexts: boundary descriptions (Num 13:21, 34:8; Josh 13:5; Judg 3:3), Davidic conquests and alliances (2 Sam 8:9; 1 Kgs 8:65), Northern Kingdom expansion (2 Kgs 14:25/28), Assyrian conquest accounts (2 Kgs 17:24/30, 18:34, 19:13, 23:33, 25:21), and Chronicles parallels (1 Chr 13:5, 18:3/9; 2 Chr 8:4). All morphological variants (bare form, with prepositions מִן/בְּ/לְ, directional ה-) refer to the same geographic entity. Multilingual glosses are remarkably consistent in transliterating: Hamath/Hamat/Chamat (Eng/Deu/Fra/Spa), حَمَاة (Arb), हमात/खमात (Hin), 하맛/하마 (Kor).
